courses.name: Special Topics in Technology: Continual Learning in AI

prep.text: Review Tuesday’s replay/rehearsal framing: new learning must improve the new context without erasing behavior that still matters
Come ready to compare four retention designs - replay, regularization, isolation, and modular routing - against risk, memory, privacy, capacity, and rollback constraints
Skim the uploaded Lecture 7 deck before revisiting the in-class factory exercises

takeaways: Regularization adds a preservation penalty to new-task error. EWC protects parameters in proportion to their estimated importance, but the penalty strength is a business and safety choice, not a universal optimum.

Isolation freezes a stable base and gives a new context separate capacity such as an adapter, head, mask, or branch. It reduces interference and makes rollback easier, but capacity grows with contexts.

Modularity adds routing: the system must pick the right component at runtime. It works well when contexts have conflicting mappings and reliable metadata; routing uncertainty needs a fallback or human input.

Choose the simplest design that fits the evidence: shared updates with replay or regularization for compatible mappings; isolated modules for conflicting mappings; always gate release on adaptation, retention, routing, latency, and rollback tests.
